builder_plan.scenario: A support or data assistant repeats work across related customer requests.
builder_plan.change: Try the paper's memory change in a replay of past tasks, with separate memory per customer.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current memory pipeline plus a no-memory control using the same agent.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Task success, stale memories, retrieval misses, response latency, and all memory maintenance costs.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: When Should Agents Remember? Falsification-Gated Self-Evolution for LLM Agents
summary: The method replaces direct writing of episode-derived lessons into persistent agent memory by treating each candidate lesson as a structured hypothesis that is applied only temporarily and tested before commitment. It costs extra inference calls and engineering complexity to construct hypotheses, run target-transfer, falsification, and archived-regression probes, and maintain a gated memory lifecycle. It can fail if probes are weak or unrepresentative, if verifier feedback is noisy or misaligned, or if the added gating rejects useful updates or still admits harmful ones under distribution shift.
rationale: The approach is relevant to production agents with persistent memory, but its benefits depend on verifier quality and benchmark-specific probe design, so constrained teams should validate it narrowly before adoption.
technique: Falsification-gated memory updates for LLM agents

It costs extra inference calls and engineering complexity to construct hypotheses, run target-transfer, falsification, and archived-regression probes, and maintain a gated memory lifecycle. It can fail if probes are weak or unrepresentative, if verifier feedback is noisy or misaligned, or if the added gating rejects useful updates or still admits harmful ones under distribution shift.

FGSE reports 39.8% WebArena success, 78.8% AppWorld average completion, and 0.724/0.487 Pass^1 on τ-Retail/τ-Airline, with falsification failures reduced to 5.0%, regression damage to 1.3%, and harmful committed updates to 3.6%.
